page.metaTitle: Hotel Price Tracker & Rate Drop Alerts | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Track hotel prices and catch rate drops automatically. Monitor Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia, and direct hotel pages for the right window to book.
page.h1: Hotel price tracker with rate drop alerts
page.subtitle: Hotel rates change daily based on demand, season, and inventory. Set up a monitor on the rooms you're considering and get alerted when the price drops.
page.intro: WebMonitor.fyi watches hotel pricing across Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia, and direct hotel websites. The hotel price tracker fires an alert when a watched room drops below your target — usually because of demand softening, inventory release, or a promotional code activating. Useful for flexible travelers, business travel teams, and anyone planning a stay months in advance.

features.title: Multi-platform tracking
features.body: Same dates, multiple booking sites — get alerts from whichever platform drops first.

features.title: Date-flexible search monitoring
features.body: Track a search results URL across a date range and surface the cheapest matching night.

features.title: Direct-vs-OTA comparison
features.body: Run parallel monitors on the hotel's own website and a third-party booking site. Direct often beats OTA pricing but not always.

features.title: Inventory release alerts
features.body: Hotels release new inventory blocks in batches. Get notified when previously sold-out dates open back up.

steps.title: Paste the booking URL
steps.body: A specific room rate page or a search results URL with dates and guest count locked.

steps.title: Write the criterion
steps.body: Examples: "Alert me when the per-night rate drops below $180." "Notify me if any room category opens for these dates." "Let me know if a non-refundable rate is cheaper than my current refundable booking."

steps.title: Pick a frequency
steps.body: Daily checks for trips months out; hourly in the final two weeks before travel when rates often move.

steps.title: Receive alerts
steps.body: Email is the standard channel for travel — the windows are rarely sub-hour.

useCases: Catch rate drops on a flexible booking you can rebook at the lower price
Watch the same hotel across Booking.com, Hotels.com, and the hotel's direct site
Track conference hotel-block availability for a trip months out
Monitor a search across flexible dates for the cheapest matching night
Catch member-rate or promotional codes the moment they activate
page.limits: WebMonitor sees publicly rendered pricing. Loyalty-tier-locked rates that only show after login (some Hilton, Marriott, Hyatt member rates) are outside scope. Pricing that varies by user cookie or IP location may show different values than what you see logged in.

faq.q: Should I cancel and rebook if the rate drops?
faq.a: WebMonitor sends the alert; the cancel-and-rebook decision is yours, and depends on the cancellation policy of your existing booking. Refundable rates usually allow this; non-refundable do not. Some OTAs and hotel direct sites offer price-match policies that don't require a rebook.

faq.q: Can I track flight prices the same way?
faq.a: Yes — paste a flight search URL from Google Flights, Kayak, or a specific airline's page. Flight pricing changes more frequently than hotels, so hourly checks are common.

faq.q: Does this work for vacation rentals (Airbnb, Vrbo)?
faq.a: Yes. Any publicly accessible booking page works — vacation rentals included.

faq.q: How early should I start monitoring?
faq.a: Three to six months out is the typical sweet spot for non-peak travel. For peak dates (holidays, major events), start monitoring as soon as the inventory window opens, often nine to twelve months out.
